analysis:
I found no qualifying security regression in the supplied evidence, but part of the PR is unreviewed.

QwenTensorParallelDecodeBench.swift is a developer bench. It adds optional `layerStride` and `buildsAhead` parameters, plus a `run` helper that wraps the stride in a task-local. Inputs are bounded: width 1..8, 255 runs at most, and build-ahead only with folded control. It logs timings and an 8-byte token digest, not prompt content or keys. The bench uses fixed synthetic prompts, so A-001 is not touched. Both ranks still derive the same request IDs and prompts.

QwenTensorParallelLaunch.swift (head lines 83-104) adds `decodeLayerStride = 8` and `decodeSubmissions`. The `decodeSubmissions` guards handle stride <= 0 and layers <= 0. The comment says the stride is evaluation order only and that ranks need not agree on it. The stride is deliberately not in the launch agreement digest (`agreementVersion` is unchanged at v5). Each rank's logits and committed state are meant to keep their bits at any stride. A rank-divergent stride could in principle affect collective ordering and availability. The comment says collectives stay in layer order, but I could not verify this. The environment-variable gate DARKBLOOM_QWEN_TP_WINDOW_LAYER_SUBMISSION (MTPTarget lines 120-125) is unchanged and still bound into the load agreement, so no new rank-divergence path appears there.

QwenTensorParallelMTPTarget.swift has only a comment change (lines 95-97). No behavior change.

QwenTensorParallelNativeBatchExecutor.swift (2d4a6524f44af431:0) is metadata only. Its patch excerpt is truncated and no source text was supplied. It adds `buildsAhead`, `submitDecode`, and a split of `select` into `buildSelection` and `readSelection`. I could not examine this path. Open questions for integration are whether build-ahead submits work before the cancellation, control and error checks, and whether it keeps the fail-closed behavior in MLX.withError/check. Also open: whether it preserves lane/KV frontier consistency on paged hosts and keeps collective ordering identical across ranks, because a mismatch could deadlock or stall (A-018 availability). These are unverified contracts, not findings, so needs_deeper_review is true.
